svg.title: What all 4,294,967,296 keys scored
svg.desc: Two log-scale histograms of every score in the sweep. In the first, the noise piles up on the left between minus 1851.8 and minus 1826.8, then 206 log-units pass with nothing in them at all, then the key stands alone on the right. The second magnifies the noise: 4,249,795,476 keys, 98.95 percent of the space, share one bin at the floor, twenty-four bins above it are empty, and the rest thins from millions a bin down to one.
svg.text: Every key in the space, counted into bins of 0.1 log-units.
Height is how many keys scored that much. The scale is logarithmic: each line up is a hundredfold.
206.39 log-units, and not one key in them
all landing on exactly the same score
A candidate whose decryption holds no run of four letters is charged the floor on every window, so it
lands on the same number as all the others. The twenty-four bins directly above it are empty, because
recognising a single quadgram is worth about 2.5 log-units and there is no smaller step to take.
